overall: The AG found three violations: no timely response to the open session minutes request, improper handling of the executive session minutes request, and failure to release executive session minutes after the litigation ended.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested open session minutes of a February 16 meeting; the Commission never responded to the request within 10 days.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Commission has still not responded to the complainant's request for open session minutes, we find a violation.

allegations.summary: Counsel denied the request for executive session minutes before the Commission reviewed them to decide whether they could be released.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to appropriately respond to a request for executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes stayed withheld after the litigation ended, when the Commission decided not to appeal the court decision.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the executive session purpose has expired and the Commission can no longer rely on the Open Meeting Law for withholding them from the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint also sought audio recordings and emails, which are the subject of a pending Supervisor of Records appeal, so they fall outside this review.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we limit our review to the request for minutes, only.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements; we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law;
Provide the complainant with a copy of the open session minutes of the February 16, 2016 meeting within 10 days of receipt of this letter; and
Publicly release the executive session minutes of its February 16, 2016 executive session meeting.
